To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CPs and MOF materials have been shown to be efficient in nonlinear optics (NLO) and photonic processes; the design of CPs and metal-organic framework (MOF) materials with optimized optical properties can be achieved by the judicious choice of metal ions, linkers and/or additives; the optical properties of CPs/MOFs can be further enhanced by the introduction of optically-active molecules; the photophysics of CPs and/or MOFs can be tuned by the

(1) the NLO properties (two-photon and SHG) of CPs and, especially, MOFs can be tuned by the choice of the building blocks, (2) the upconversion efficiency of the TEM process in MOFs is strongly dependent on the porosity and the choice of the host material and (3) MOFs can act as efficient lasing media.

CPs and MOF can exhibit: (i) nonlinear optical (NOL) properties (e.g. two-photon absorption (TPA), third-harmonic generation and second-harmoni generation (SHG)), (ii) upconversion via triplet-triplet energy migration (TTA-UC) and (iii) lasing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials with novel properties and functions.
a wide range of optical processes in MOFs, including two-, three- (and multi-) photon absorption, upconversion and stimulated emission.
a broad range of nonlinear optical phenomena, upconversion and stimulated emission in CPs and metal-organic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optical properties of CPs/MOFs are not only determined by their structure and composition but also by the interplay between them, which is the main driving force for the emergence of new phenomena.
CPs and MOF materials are not only a playground for fundamental research in nonlinear optics but they also provide a basis for a wide range of practical applications.
the field of CPs and, particularly, MOFs, as materials for optical applications, has just started to bloom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CPs and MOF materials are promising candidates for the realization of novel nonlinear optical phenomena, and that the field is still in its infancy.

MOFs and CPs are versatile materials that are capable of exhibiting a wide range of optical phenomena, and that their properties are largely predetermined by the nature of the building blocks and by the way in which they are assembled.
the field of NLO, upconversion and photonic properties of CPs/MOFs is still in its infancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the already established optical properties of CPs/MOFs, the field of nonlinear optics and photoluminescence in these materials is in its infancy and is still in need of further development.
the optical properties of CPs, MOFs and MOF composites can be tuned in a controlled manner by judicious choice of structural building blocks and their mutual arrangement.
, despite a vast number of reports on the optical properties of CPs, MOFs and their hybrids, there is still room to explore the full potential of these materials.
